title: An Enhanced-Frequency-Splitting-Based Wireless Power and Data Transfer System Achieving 60.2% End-to-End Efficiency and 1 Mb/s Data Rate with a Sub-cm RX Coil for Miniaturized Implants
problem: Miniaturized implantable devices face a fundamental trade-off between power transfer efficiency (PTE) and data rate (DR) in wireless power and data transfer (WPDT) systems, worsened by coil size constraints; frequency-splitting-based WPDT reduces this trade-off but still requires large receiver coils to achieve critical coupling coefficient, limiting implant miniaturization.
motivation: Implantable medical devices must minimize invasiveness and complexity; WPDT is the critical bottleneck as receiver coil size directly limits device miniaturization, and conventional frequency-splitting systems remain coil-size limited.
method: The system uses a receiver circuit made of a capacitor and inductor (an LC tank) with switchable resistance. By switching this resistance, it implements link-load isolation—reducing the load that the power transfer link must drive, which decreases the critical coupling coefficient (the minimum magnetic connection needed between coils). The system operates at two frequencies (f_H and f_L) using frequency-shift keying (data encoding by switching between frequencies) to transmit both power and data, with efficiency remaining flat across this frequency range, enabling receiver coils smaller than a centimeter.
key_novelty: The key innovation is a switchable receiver circuit that dynamically isolates power transfer from data transmission, achieving a 10-fold reduction in receiver coil size while preserving the efficiency of frequency-splitting wireless power transfer.
contributions: 60.2% end-to-end power transfer efficiency with dual-frequency FSK
1 Mb/s data rate without power-rate trade-off
Sub-cm receiver coil (10x size reduction) enabling device miniaturization
Frequency splitting enhancement through dynamic LC tank control
limitations: Abstract does not discuss maximum transmission distance, power level delivered to load (POL), biological safety (SAR limits), frequency band used, or implant miniaturization limits.
primary_theme: dynamic link-load isolation for coil-size-reduced wireless implant power transfer
